claims.statement: This is OMIV's first public ecosystem case study; it followed a public technical exchange in which Daniel Han suggested Gemma 4 E2B IT as the first reproducible case, and OMIV independently executed and analyzed it.

The fixed source was google/gemma-4-E2B-it at revision 3e22461f65e89153144f8adb70e3b8c2cc9845a7 with 9 files, 10278849571 bytes, and manifest b73a8a4dd3aa11c51f5dcc06e13dbdecbbcd1f7eaa55518febe8ffeaf10d8a75; the canonical source manifest remained unchanged during export.
Retained execution evidence records one successful Q8_0 export and verified local artifact custody.
The main artifact is a regular 4954594880-byte file with SHA-256 fbf3f93d603e92dbcf00742163cc3018b9bf8fbfbcf87158cc836e5ed0bc9455.
The main artifact is GGUF v3 with 51 metadata entries and 601 tensors: 318 Q8_0 and 283 F32.
The mmproj artifact is a regular 986833792-byte file with SHA-256 e00089a95d2dc85c71f249bd83760e348f721757318802ddb889c65ec64eae3c.
The mmproj artifact is GGUF v3 with 39 metadata entries and 1411 tensors: 247 BF16 and 1164 F32.
All parsed tensor byte ranges were within their files and non-overlapping.

Current artifact size and SHA-256 identities match retained historical C1 observations, preserving HISTORICAL_C1_MATCH; historical C1 bytes are unavailable, and no new direct C1/C2 file comparison was performed.
Neither target GGUF metadata inventory contained the exact source revision.
The main and mmproj artifacts have a moderate contextual association based on shared export context and compatible exporter and model-family/projector-role metadata.
No cryptographic or format-native main/mmproj binding was observed, and the shared name Work Copy has low identifying power.
The tokenizer_config work-copy diff contains 195 JSON-pointer changes: 181 additions and 14 removals; this lineage event is not automatically a bug.
Every repeated deterministic OMIV-native output used in A1 was byte-identical across the paired runs.
Semantic fidelity and numerical quantization fidelity were not evaluated, and Q8_0 type classification is not a quality result.
Structural validation and export success do not by themselves establish runtime compatibility.
Missing source-revision metadata is a provenance-observability gap, not proof of incorrect model weights.
Weak main/mmproj binding is an artifact-association gap, not proof of incompatibility.

A1 found complete native coverage for custody, core GGUF structure, scalar metadata, tensor inventories, structural comparison, and deterministic reporting, with partial, glue-only, retained-evidence-only, or unsupported coverage for several lineage, binding, and fidelity questions.
A1 was completely offline and did not load a model, run inference, invoke an exporter, use a GPU, or evaluate tensor payload values for semantic or numerical fidelity.

This study did not determine whether the observed provenance, association, or tokenizer-lineage behavior originated in Unsloth, llama.cpp tooling, GGUF conventions, llm-compressor, or the surrounding export workflow.
